description: PM-11 coherence: the Plan Editor and the Battle Simulator survive being entered, left, and entered again. Both are unusual enough to be worth pinning. The Plan Editor deliberately holds the DEPLOYMENT phase open instead of letting it advance, and the Simulator is an autoload CanvasLayer that outlives the scene changes its own games cause — either could leave state behind that breaks the second visit, and neither would be caught by a test that only ever opens them once. The scenario opens each, leaves via its own exit path, returns to the menu, and opens it again, asserting the second visit is as good as the first.

steps.script: return str(tree.current_scene.name)

var pm = tree.root.get_node_or_null("PhaseManager")
return "%s|%s" % [str(tree.current_scene.name), str(pm.is_plan_editor_session())]
return str(tree.current_scene.name)

# The flag DOES survive the exit — meta.game_config keeps the editor's
# config until something replaces it, so on the menu it still reads true.
# That is recorded rather than asserted away, because the invariant that
# actually matters is the next one: a normal game started afterwards must
# not be a plan-editor session. MainMenu replaces meta.game_config wholesale
# when Start Game is pressed, so the staleness cannot reach a real game — and
# the next steps prove that rather than trusting the code read.
var pm = tree.root.get_node_or_null("PhaseManager")
print("SCENARIO pm11 editor flag on the menu after exit: %s (stale, harmless — see next step)" % str(pm.is_plan_editor_session()))
return "recorded"

# THE invariant: a normal game started straight after the editor is not a
# plan-editor session. If it were, deployment would hold open and the game
# would never start properly.
var pm = tree.root.get_node_or_null("PhaseManager")
print("SCENARIO pm11 normal game after editor: scene=%s editor_session=%s" % [str(tree.current_scene.name), str(pm.is_plan_editor_session())])
return "%s|%s" % [str(tree.current_scene.name), str(pm.is_plan_editor_session())]

# Back to the menu the way a player would, so the rest of the scenario
# carries on from a known place.
var main = tree.current_scene
if main.has_method("_on_main_menu_requested"):
	main._on_main_menu_requested()
	return "requested"
return "no menu path"
return str(tree.current_scene.name)

# Visit 2: same again. This is the actual test.
var m = tree.current_scene
var army = -1
for i in range(m.army_options.size()):
	if str(m.army_options[i].id) == "recon_stomps":
		army = i
m.player1_dropdown.selected = army
m.player1_dropdown.emit_signal("item_selected", army)
var zone = -1
for i in range(m.plan_editor_zone_dropdown.item_count):
	if m.plan_editor_zone_dropdown.get_item_text(i).begins_with("Hammer"):
		zone = i
m.plan_editor_zone_dropdown.selected = zone
return "ready"

var pm = tree.root.get_node_or_null("PhaseManager")
return "%s|%s" % [str(tree.current_scene.name), str(pm.is_plan_editor_session())]

var sim = tree.root.get_node_or_null("PlanSimulatorUI")
return str(sim.visible)

var sim = tree.root.get_node_or_null("PlanSimulatorUI")
return "%s|%s" % [str(sim.visible), str(tree.current_scene.name)]

# Visit 2 of the simulator — the one that would catch a half-torn-down panel.
var sim = tree.root.get_node_or_null("PlanSimulatorUI")
sim.open()
return "opened"
